title: WP-000/N06.9.1.5: Retire coverage, active-perception, manual-pilot, and physical-world legibility contracts
description:
## Background

This task retires COMPASS, active perception, pilot guidance, spatial-handle, and shared-cockpit contracts. The product guides an authorized human pilot toward evidence deficits; it does not command an aircraft or convert a high score into authority. Guidance is successful only when observed capture produces verified decision-relevant evidence gain under safety/privacy/budget constraints.

## Binding Requirement Inventory

1. Coverage is a first-class, claim-specific evidence product. Deterministic cells/samples bind geometry/region, supporting frames/rays, observation and source/time diversity, view angles, baseline/parallax, pixel density/ground sampling distance, blur/exposure/compression, occlusion/dynamic fraction, depth/pose uncertainty, semantic detectability, privacy authorization, and covered/partial/unknown/excluded/unseen status.
2. Geometric coverage does not imply semantic detectability: a facade may be covered while a small spigot or thin cable remains indeterminate. Unauthorized or inaccessible space is excluded/unknown, never empty.
3. Before stable geometry, provisional coverage uses frusta, overlap, provisional depth and view-sphere bins with explicit camera/basis uncertainty and freshness. It is later reprojected to converged geometry without rewriting the provisional history.
4. A CoverageCertificate binds anchor/geometry generation, spatial domain, task/profile, cell policy/resolution, quality/detectability thresholds, covered/partial/unknown/excluded areas, support, uncertainty/limitations, expiry/freshness, and content root. Completeness and absence claims require a compatible certificate.
5. Next-best-view candidates optimize surface novelty, triangulation baseline, incidence diversity, loop closure, target detail/resolution, occlusion relief, scale/calibration witness visibility, route/time/battery/storage/operator cost, safety, privacy, property/geofence/no-fly exclusions, and a do-nothing option. Methods may use deterministic greedy submodular/set-cover, graph/visibility search, or learned advisory ranking with explicit approximation/complexity/ties.
6. A candidate is a proposal containing objective/question bundle, suggested viewpoint region and camera orientation, affected surfaces/assets, expected information gain and assumptions, route/time/battery estimate, quality conditions, risk/exclusions, exact evidence basis, score components, counterfactual/invalidators, stop/abort conditions, and a statement that it is not a flight command.
7. Capture profiles include rapid exterior overview; high-quality facade/roof/terrain; utility inspection; entrance/accessibility/path; before/after change; privacy-restricted/redacted; calibration/scale target. Each specifies overlap, speed/angular motion, view diversity, detail, ontology targets, source settings, quality thresholds, budgets and exclusions as goals—not guarantees.
8. Operator presentation shows source health/gaps, provisional trajectory/map, quality warnings, covered/uncertain/unseen regions, target observations/unresolved hypotheses, scale/calibration, highest-value next views, battery/time/storage budget, original-recording state and later verification, plus an explicit degraded mode. Warnings are deterministic, prioritized, rate-limited and hysteretic rather than noisy raw model output.
9. Human-legible SpatialHandles bind frame and anchor, landmark/region/asset relation, viewpoint/orientation, tolerance, units/scale status, geometry/coverage uncertainty, privacy scope, validity/expiry and resolution path. Bare “left/right/north side” language is refused when the frame or landmark is ambiguous.
10. Pilot guidance compiles only through `fdgr.propose`, then an authorized human decides whether to act. The singular Decision Frame carries objective/questions, current evidence, alternatives/do-nothing, recommendation, risk, budgets, proof/recovery and typed next steps. Guidance remains authority-free.
11. The operator may acknowledge, reject, defer, modify within registered bounds, or report impossibility. Acknowledgement is not execution. Observed execution requires capture evidence and device/source state; verified evidence gain recomputes coverage/question/uncertainty on the compatible successor anchor.
12. Closed-loop state is proposed -> acknowledged/rejected/deferred -> observed/not-observed/indeterminate -> evidence verified/rejected -> objective advanced/unchanged -> next proposal or stop. Cancellation/abort, lost source, stale geometry, changed weather/battery, safety/privacy conflict, and no beneficial candidate produce typed fallback and reconciliation.
13. Initial safety authority stays with the human. Suggestions are not guaranteed routes. The operator retains responsibility for lawful flight, line of sight, obstacles, people, neighboring property, weather, battery, device warnings and boundaries. Camera/gimbal effects, if separately admitted, do not imply navigation; autonomous/assisted flight requires its own future constitutional gate.
14. Success is minimum-cost safe progress: information gain is measured against the question/coverage deficit and total cost includes tokens, compute, bytes, pilot time, battery, risk and recovery burden. title: WP-000/N06.9.1.6: Retire custody, archive, repair, retention, search, report, and export contracts
description:
## Background

This task retires ORIGIN, VAULT, storage, archive, repair, search, report, and export contracts. Custody means immutable, retrievable, policy-authorized evidence linked by verified roots—not “uploaded,” “in a database,” or “a bucket exists.” Derived indexes and publications remain rebuildable projections over one evidence universe.

## Binding Requirement Inventory

1. Storage roles remain separate: small transactional ledger; immutable CAS and manifests; operation-owned unpublished staging; rebuildable indexes/caches/thumbnails/model caches; verified local/remote replicas and repair material; policy-scoped exports. No SQLite file, directory, graph store or bucket is the whole truth; a published root connects roles.
2. Object classes cover raw chunks/logical source, packet/frame/timeline, clock/calibration/transform, model artifact/proposal, geometry tile/mesh/uncertainty/coverage, semantic/scene graph, report/export, receipt/doctor/qualification and repair symbol. Headers bind magic/version, domain/type, logical length, compression/encryption wrapper, child/chunk policy, digest/checksum, flags and bounds.
3. Staging is capability-scoped and operation-owned. Publication validates child closure/digests, canonical manifests, type/size/depth/count, path/link authority, durability policy, temporary-write absence, root identity, plan/witness/fence and cancellation; only then atomically advances a branch/root and records a receipt. Crash at every step exposes either the old complete root or the new complete root, never a mixture.
4. The reference ledger defines semantics before FrankenSQLite. A future admitted ledger stores roots, indexes, intents/plans/witnesses/idempotency/leases/effects/obligations, claim evidence, archive/retention/repair and work high-waters; blobs stay in CAS and external/process/network/large fsync work occurs before a short validating commit.
5. FrankenFS is an admitted custody adapter only after reference parity for rooted capabilities, snapshots/COW, durability epochs, crash evidence, repair plans and root publication. It cannot redefine FDGR identity/publication.
6. Archive classes distinguish irreplaceable originals/calibration/scale/human confirmations; authoritative ledgers/roots/clock/calibration/geometry/semantics/receipts; warm analysis; preview/cache; model artifacts; derived exports. Retention strength and repair allocation follow replaceability, replay cost, license/privacy and active obligations.
7. S3-compatible object keys are provider-neutral and immutable from FDGR identity/domain; branch heads use a separate conditional/append-only protocol. Multipart work is reserve obligation -> registered part size -> per-part digest/idempotency -> list/reconcile -> complete -> lookup metadata -> full or deterministic-sample readback -> FDGR digest -> verified replica receipt. ETag/provider version/acknowledgement is observation only.
8. Credentials are narrow endpoint/bucket/prefix/method/time/byte capabilities, never serialized into plans/evidence/worker manifests/support bundles. Provider profiles capture part size, checksum, write-rate, abort/object-lock and consistency semantics rather than assuming uniform S3 behavior.
9. ATP transfers immutable content-addressed object graphs with resumable symbols, path racing/bonded donors, repair symbols, manifest/child scheduling, receiver verification, budgets and cancellation. RaptorQ allocation is policy-driven for irreplaceable or expensive content; repair symbols have identities/custody. Neither transports commands, credentials or generic effect RPC.
10. Encryption separates plaintext logical identity from ciphertext representation identity. Policies bind algorithm/profile, authenticated manifests, privacy/key domain, provider observation, key custody/rotation/revocation and restore verification. Rotation creates wrappers/manifests rather than rewriting plaintext identity; lost/wrong/expired key makes availability explicitly degraded.
11. `doctor` performs bounded scans and reports findings. A sealed repair plan binds basis/retention, missing/corrupt/unverified objects, candidate replicas/symbols, exact reads/writes/deletes, expected result, budgets/privacy/provider capabilities and digest. Apply revalidates basis, reconciles ambiguous remote state and never writes different bytes under an existing identity.
12. Restore drills declare loss scenarios: index-only, local CAS, ledger with roots, one provider, corrupt chunks, staging plus indeterminate upload, or complete host. They reconstruct retained roots, verify closure/digests, reopen history, rebuild indexes, render reports and sample media/geometry/semantic claims. A backup never restored earns no readiness claim.
13. Retention/deletion marks all retained branches/roots, owner/legal policy, obligations/idempotency, replica/repair dependencies, report/export provenance, model/license replay artifacts and privacy requests. Delete computes a graph cut, blockers and surviving reconstructibility, obtains required approval, seals/revalidates, deletes with lookup/reconcile, rebuilds state, verifies privacy effect/surviving roots and publishes tombstone/receipt. Garbage collection cannot bypass critical delete authority.
14. Search is a derived, anchor-bound accelerator. Exact lexical/vector/spatial/temporal/graph filters remain distinct from ranking. Progressive events expose accepted/partial/complete/cancelled/failed state, coverage/completeness, omitted shards/sources and stable continuation; stale indexes are detectable and rebuildable. Model summaries/rerankers remain proposals with exact evidence links.
15. Reports compile from one typed IR carrying anchors, claims, epistemic status, uncertainty, coverage, units/frames/scale, provenance, privacy and omissions. Deterministic exports include reports, measurements, point/mesh/glTF/geospatial and redacted products as policy-scoped derivatives with manifests; appearance does not become geometry and redaction is verified beyond EXIF removal.

## Translation Work

Map the inventory to WP-003/WP-004/WP-024/WP-025/WP-028 and relevant agent/qualification tasks; object/replica/repair/retention/search/report/export schemas; GATE-001/GATE-002/GATE-012..GATE-014; and public doctor/query/explain/propose/commit/watch behavior. Every adapter retains reference semantics and an honest current maturity.

## Test Plan

Unit/property/differential tests cover object/chunk closure, root-last publication, adapter/reference parity, multipart reconciliation, checksums/readback, ATP missing-block repair, encryption wrappers, repair seals, mark/cut deletion, search completeness/continuation and report determinism. title: WP-000/N06.9.1.7: Retire the complete agent operating system, shared cockpit, handoff, and accretion contracts
description:
## Background

This task retires every agent-facing constitutional document. The system is the loop visible from the operating agent's seat, not a set of crate APIs. A cold agent must orient, choose the minimum-cost safe next step, act only with explicit authority, verify semantic completion, recover, and leave a sufficient handoff without reading source or replaying a transcript.

## Binding Requirement Inventory

1. One operating loop is canonical: open session/compatibility -> orient -> focus/query -> propose -> compare -> commit -> watch -> verify/reconcile/cancel as needed -> explain -> handoff. Subsystem verbs are typed affordance templates compiled through this waist, not new top-level authority.
2. The abstraction tower spans physical evidence/signals; observations; entities/relations; claims/coverage; questions/objectives; plans/obligations; decisions/episodes; campaigns/missions/policy. Upward summaries retain anchors, epistemic class and omissions; downward expansion resolves to exact handles and required authority. No sideways component owns a competing mission or mutation plane.
3. Four synchronized ledgers are always visible or reachable: truth/evidence/claims; purpose/objectives/questions/terminal predicates; work/plans/obligations/effects/progress; custody/availability/retention/privacy/qualification. A turn cannot imply coherence if these bases are incompatible.
4. Open-session negotiation freezes protocol/schema versions, lineage/branch/anchor, capabilities/authority, privacy, profile/projection, token/compute/byte/time budgets, continuation basis and compatibility. Unknown mandatory versions/projections fail closed with a safe repair.
5. Every success, progress, and error uses one Agent Turn Packet spine: protocol/schema, turn/session, anchor vector/basis, epistemic class, active work, objective/question state, four-ledger summaries, result/error, uncertainty, coverage/completeness/omissions, authority/capabilities, budgets/cost/pressure, attention, affordances/typed next steps, recovery/continuation, provenance and evidence receipt. Error packets preserve useful state.
6. Profiles are pulse, briefing, tactical, pilot, forensic and fail-closed custom. Pulse is a cheap heartbeat, briefing is cold-arrival orientation, tactical/pilot require focus, forensic requires explicit scope. Token ranges are targets, never truncation permission for mandatory safety/authority/coverage/recovery fields.
7. Mission/objective/question graphs bind parent purpose, exact anchor/domain, terminal predicate, value-of-information, evidence deficit, decision boundary, support/counterevidence, coverage/detectability, cost/risk, blockers, status and stopping reason. A dominating question is one whose resolution changes the decision frontier; activity without objective progress is not progress.
8. Context packs bind Pack DNA: anchor/basis, profile/projections, focus, mandatory safety classes, selection candidates, token/byte budget, redundancy/diversity, omitted classes, producer/version, continuation and digest. Selection may be submodular/adaptive only after correctness; it cannot omit privacy, authority, scale, coverage, custody, recovery or active-work facts.
9. Attention is scheduled epistemic debt. Interrupts have class, severity, evidence, affected decision/objective, cost of delay, expiry/freshness, acknowledgement/suppression/hysteresis and shared-work opportunity. Stable ordering prevents alert churn; accepting debt is explicit and never erases it.
10. Affordances are typed and basis-bound. Recommendations, memories and model output are authority-free. Candidate sets share one basis and include do-nothing; each plan binds expected outcome, assumptions, invalidators, cost/risk, obligations/effects, witnesses, recovery and terminal proof. Compare returns a Pareto frontier without hiding dominated tradeoffs.
11. Commit revalidates basis, capability, policy, budget, witnesses, idempotency and plan seal before creating owned obligations. It never executes an unsealed recommendation. Commit-time drift returns typed stale-basis recovery, not an implicit replan.
12. Watch reports semantic milestones rather than polling noise: accepted/started/observed/verified/published/objective-complete, active obligations, pressure, blockers, cancellations/drains, failures/indeterminate state, receipts and safe next step. Adapter/process exit is never semantic completion.
13. Explain traverses claims, decisions, scores, evidence, counterevidence, omissions, roots, policy, candidate comparison and recovery. Query is bounded and anchor-complete. 17. Handoff capsules are sealed, compact, authority-free continuity: compatible anchor, objective/questions, decisions/rationale, active work/obligations, uncertainty/coverage, budgets, blockers/risks, evidence roots, safe next steps, recovery and omissions. Resumption revalidates everything; credentials/leases/capabilities never transfer by prose.
18. Shared observations reduce work only when basis/privacy/authority are compatible.
19. 6. description:
## Background

FastMCP Rust is admitted only as a replaceable transport and presentation adapter. FDGR semantics, schemas, authority, idempotency, obligations, recovery, and evidence live below it. A convenient framework must not become a second agent protocol or leak into core crates.

## Technical Approach

- **Admitted profile:** pin an exact source identity/version/feature set and approved transitive closure under the dependency policy. Only `fdgr-mcp` may depend on it. Record compatibility epoch, protocol capabilities, known gaps, license, and fallback.
- **Handler-context mapping:** translate MCP request/session/auth/cancel/deadline/progress fields into the canonical `Cx`, Agent Turn Packet anchor, profile, capability, request ID, budgets, and trace identity. Missing or conflicting context fails closed; handlers do not invent roots.
- **Cancellation and tasks:** MCP cancellation requests region cancellation and returns an honest accepted/partial/cancelled/indeterminate state after drain/reconcile rules. Long work creates canonical FDGR obligations/tasks; framework task handles are projections, not truth.
- **Stable narrow tool mapping:** expose exactly the eleven operations with registry-derived schemas. Domain resources/prompts may improve discovery but cannot add a mutation verb, skip propose/commit/watch, or encode transport-specific semantic states.
- **Large artifacts and streaming:** exchange content-addressed resource links/manifests and bounded progressive events, not unbounded inline blobs. Apply backpressure, chunk/order/checksum/root verification, continuation, cancellation, and typed truncation.
- **Error/outcome mapping:** map typed FDGR error/status/recovery/last-valid-packet fields losslessly to MCP results. Protocol/transport failure remains distinct from request acceptance, effect, verified output, publication, and semantic completion.
- **Cache/session isolation:** keys include tenant/project/session, exact anchor roots, capability/privacy/profile, schema/model/policy epoch, and query parameters. No cross-session leakage, global mutable truth, hidden stale result, or cache-created authority.
- **Replaceability test:** run the same semantic conformance suite through direct core, CLI/NDJSON, FastMCP, and a minimal test adapter. Canonical requests/results/errors/receipts must match modulo registered presentation-only fields.
- **Security posture:** bounded request bodies and outputs, strict schemas, rooted resource capabilities, taint handling, no arbitrary file/network/command execution, secrets isolated, network disabled by default for workers, authorization before existence disclosure, and adversarial protocol corpus.
- **Qualification/dogfooding:** cold-agent discovery/orient/query/propose/commit/watch/cancel/explain/handoff/doctor scenarios, reconnect/resume, progressive artifacts, multi-session isolation, cancellation, overload, and malformed input run locally with exact receipts. Hosted badges are informational only.

Reject FastMCP types in pure/domain crates, framework-owned canonical sessions/tasks, auto-generated extra verbs, direct model/device calls, transport retry of indeterminate effects, opaque string errors, ambient global cache, or completion inferred from an MCP success envelope.

## Acceptance Criteria

Removing or replacing FastMCP changes only `fdgr-mcp` and presentation receipts. The eleven operations, schemas, states, authorities, obligations, recovery, and digests remain stable. Cancellation drains, artifacts verify, sessions isolate, errors map losslessly, security tests pass, and cold agents can operate without transport-specific knowledge.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_fastmcp_boundary_contract.py` and `scripts/e2e/mcp_replaceability_conformance.sh`. Test schema parity for all operations/profiles/errors; direct/CLI/MCP/minimal-adapter differential; cancel before/during/after dispatch; long task progress/resume; chunk corruption/reorder/duplication/overrun; cross-session/tenant cache probes; stale anchors; auth/privacy noninterference; malformed/oversized requests; resource path escape; server restart; lost response; and framework removal build fence.

Logs retain transport/version/source-closure IDs, session/turn/request/effect/obligation/anchor IDs, `Cx` budgets/deadlines/cancel, schema and capability roots, chunks/resources/digests, cache key dimensions, mappings/diffs, drain/recovery, timing, omissions, and terminal semantic verdict.

## Considerations

MCP familiarity is an ergonomic benefit, not authority. FastMCP upgrades require the same source/dependency/license and conformance evidence as any boundary dependency; unsupported framework features stay unused rather than reshaping FDGR.
acceptance_criteria: The complete FastMCP admitted profile, context/cancellation/task mapping, eleven-tool mapping, artifact streaming, errors, cache/session isolation, security, replaceability, and conformance/dogfood evidence are self-contained; fdgr-mcp remains the only boundary and never owns semantics or effects.

title: WP-000/N06.9.11: Import the complete Eidetic evidence-linked advisory-memory model
description:
## Background

FDGR agents need durable lessons across sessions, but memory is a contamination and authority risk. Eidetic is an external advisory store: it can retrieve evidence-linked practices, surprises, anti-patterns, preferences, and recovery experience to improve proposals, never rewrite canonical evidence, claims, capabilities, policy, or protocol facts.

## Technical Approach

- **Constitutional one-way boundary:** canonical FDGR episodes export sealed advisory records; memory queries return cited suggestions/context. Only canonical propose/commit/watch paths can affect FDGR. Memory service loss must reduce ergonomics, not correctness.
- **Memory classes:** procedural playbooks; failure signatures and minimized repros; recovery/repair outcomes; environment/profile compatibility observations; user/operator preferences within policy; semantic/geometry lessons; cost/performance measurements; anti-patterns and rejected shortcuts; open surprises/epistemic debt. Each class has scope, authority=`advisory`, provenance, sensitivity, retention, and promotion rules.
- **Session workflow:** orient from canonical packet first; formulate objective/question; query memory with exact project/profile/task/error/environment/basis; receive ranked candidates; inspect citations/applicability/contradictions; choose or ignore; execute only through canonical operations; record predicted versus actual result; export a new episode after terminal reconciliation.
- **Explainable context packing and Pack DNA:** select by marginal decision value, diversity, recency/decay, applicability, evidence quality, cost, and token budget. Preserve memory IDs, source episode/evidence roots, transformations, rank components, omissions, and deterministic ordering so the pack can be reproduced.
- **Confidence, decay, and outcome feedback:** confidence is a calibrated advisory score, not epistemic authority. Update from qualified helpful/harmful/redundant/misleading/uncertain outcomes; decay by class/time/environment drift; retain negative outcomes rather than averaging them away.
- **Revival conditions:** a decayed/rejected memory can re-enter only with new compatible evidence, restored environment/profile, repeated qualified success, explicit human review where required, and a new epoch. Revival never erases prior failure history.
- **Graph-aware memory:** connect tasks, errors, environments, profiles, questions, evidence, actions, outcomes, surprises, and lessons; retrieval can expand bounded neighborhoods but must not mix tenants/projects/privacy scopes or infer canonical truth.
- **Swarm/crowded-checkout use:** export reservations, ownership lessons, duplicate-work signatures, integration pitfalls, and handoff patterns as advisory coordination aids; live leases/fences and current work graph always outrank memory.
- **Automatic export templates:** versioned episode, surprise, lesson, anti-pattern, compatibility, recovery, cost, and feedback records bind exact source/toolchain/model/policy/profile/input/output roots, action/outcome, counterevidence, sensitivity, and expiry.
- **Privacy/isolation:** project/tenant/user scopes, consent and redaction, encryption/key identity, retention/deletion, no secret/raw-private payload by default, capability-aware retrieval, noninterference tests, and auditable export/query. Deletion of memory never deletes canonical evidence.
- **Promotion:** repeated held-out evidence -> shadow recommendation policy -> bounded canary with clamps -> no-regression proof -> registered policy epoch; immediate rollback. Memory itself never grants capability or resolves a claim.

Reject transcript dumping, uncited free-form “remembered facts,” global cross-project recall, memory before canonical orient, confidence as truth, direct policy mutation, stale environment advice without warning, feedback self-training without held-out gates, or deletion cascading into evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every memory record and context item has class, scope, evidence/episode roots, authority, sensitivity, applicability, confidence/decay, outcome history, and deterministic rank explanation. Privacy isolation, one-way authority, graceful absence, revival history, and promotion/rollback are proven. Cold agents can use memory without needing transcript or trusting it blindly.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_eidetic_advisory_memory.py` and `scripts/e2e/memory_context_feedback_promotion.sh`. Cover deterministic packs under token budgets, diversity/omission, helpful/harmful/redundant/misleading/uncertain feedback, decay, environment drift, stale/duplicate/conflicting items, revival, graph expansion, cross-tenant/project/privacy probes, redaction/retention/delete, service outage, malicious memory content, concurrent agents, shadow/canary/rollback, and attempted capability/claim mutation.

Logs retain memory/episode/lesson/feedback/policy IDs, tenant/project/profile/task/error/basis roots, source evidence/citations, sensitivity/capability, rank components/Pack DNA/token budget, confidence/decay/revival, prediction/outcome/surprise, promotion/rollback, omissions, digests, timing, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

Useful memory makes the agent cheaper and less repetitive; it does not shorten proof. Current canonical state, live obligations, safety, privacy, and negative evidence always outrank a remembered recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: All Eidetic memory classes, session workflow, context packing, confidence/decay/revival, graph/swarm behavior, export templates, privacy isolation, one-way authority, and promotion gates are explicit and tested; memory remains advisory and evidence-linked.

title: WP-000/N06.9.12: Import the complete Doodlestein local qualification and release model
description:
## Background

Release machinery belongs in FDGR architecture because a badge, successful build, uploaded archive, or partially completed lane cannot establish what source was tested, what artifact users received, whether installation works, or whether device/large-corpus claims are true. Doodlestein contributes twelve mechanisms.

## Technical Approach

1. **Clean source snapshot, never mutable checkout:** qualify an immutable commit/tree plus recorded dirty-state refusal; build from a clean isolated snapshot and retain source manifest/digest.
2. **Exact owned-sibling closure:** resolve every path/git/workspace sibling to immutable repository, revision, tree, dependency-policy, and license identity; reject unpublished or drifting local overrides.
3. **One qualification contract:** registries define required lanes, predicates, artifacts, environments, retry/resume rules, and release gate; local and hosted runners execute the same contract.
4. **Workflow YAML as portable job graph:** compile the qualification DAG into local and hosted execution plans with exact dependencies, inputs/outputs, capabilities, budgets, and terminal predicates; YAML is projection, not authority.
5. **Host and lane manifests:** record OS/arch/kernel, CPU/GPU/memory/storage, toolchain, dependency/model/data roots, device/profile, secrets/network posture, runner implementation, and limitations for each lane.
6. **Resumable work without blessing partial release:** each node seals inputs and receipts; valid nodes may resume by exact key, failed/unsupported nodes stay visible, and the release gate remains open until every required predicate passes at one compatible source fence.
7. **Deterministic artifact identity and promotion:** artifact IDs derive from source/toolchain/dependency/features/target/profile inputs; verify content, manifests, checksums/signatures/SBOM/provenance, then atomically promote a sealed set. Rebuild divergence blocks release.
8. **Local evidence for physical and large-corpus lanes:** device, GPU, restoration, corpus, network-disabled model, and long benchmark lanes run where required resources/data are authorized; summaries without raw receipts cannot substitute.
9. **Same-binary experiments and benchmark governance:** one binary chooses arms at runtime; prove semantic equivalence first; retain warmup/samples/outliers/statistics/hardware/policy and compare against registered thresholds without cherry-picking.
10. **Secret and credential boundaries:** least-privilege scoped credentials enter only authorized publication/signing nodes; never reach builds/tests/logs/artifacts; redact and test exfiltration paths; rotate/revoke on incident.
11. **Offline and supply-chain posture:** builds/tests use locked, vendored or verified inputs; network disabled unless a lane explicitly requires it; dependency/source/model/license/SBOM/vulnerability evidence is exact and fail-closed.
12. **Append-only auditable release evidence:** every node, retry, supersession, waiver, negative result, promotion, upload, and readback is retained. A release manifest points to the exact complete receipt DAG and artifacts.

Repository changes required by the import: machine qualification-lane and release-graph registries; clean-snapshot/source-closure tooling; local runner and portable graph exporter; host/lane/artifact/promotion/publication receipt schemas; regular cross-platform packages/installers; checksums/signatures/SBOM/provenance; installer/lifecycle smoke; public upload and independent readback; status reconciliation. Agent ergonomics is a release lane: a cold agent must discover capability, operate safely, diagnose failure, verify completion, and hand off without source archaeology.

Reject running release from a dirty checkout, treating Cargo/test success as a release, hosted-badge authority, queued/running jobs as evidence, retry that discards failure, build-only archives, ad hoc asset lists, unverified upload, hidden waivers, secret-bearing logs, or performance from different binaries.

## Acceptance Criteria

A release candidate is one immutable source closure with all mandatory local receipts, regular artifacts and installers, manifests/checksums/signatures/SBOM/provenance, lifecycle smoke, sealed promotion, public publication, and independent readback. Unsupported/failed dimensions remain visible; no partial graph can be promoted; agent ergonomics and recovery are proven.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_release_evidence_dag.py` and `scripts/e2e/local_qualification_release_readback.sh`. Cover dirty-source refusal, sibling drift, source closure, graph cycles/missing predicates, exact resume/stale cache, failed/unsupported lanes, artifact reproducibility, wrong manifest/checksum/signature/SBOM, installer install-upgrade-uninstall, device/GPU/large-corpus receipt substitution, same-binary statistics, network isolation, dependency/model drift, secret canaries, interrupted promotion/upload, missing asset, public checksum/download/readback, rollback, and cold-agent operation.

Logs retain source/sibling/toolchain/dependency/model/data/policy roots, host/lane/graph/node IDs, capabilities/budgets, command and environment allowlist, artifact/package/installer digests, checksums/signatures/SBOM/provenance, samples/statistics, secret/network posture, retries/supersessions, promotion/upload/readback, omissions, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

Qualification evidence is local and immutable; hosted automation may mirror it but cannot upgrade it. Publication is complete only when a user can independently fetch and verify the intended artifact set.
acceptance_criteria: All twelve Doodlestein mechanisms, required repository changes, rejected imitations, final admission gate, and agent-ergonomics lane are mapped to an append-only local qualification/release DAG with exact source closure, resumability, promotion, installer, supply-chain, and public readback proof.

title: WP-000/N06.9.13: Integrate all 20 cross-project compounds and reject superficial imports
description:
## Background

The highest-value FDGR ideas are compounds. Implementing each sibling mechanism independently can still fail if their join erases anchors, authority, completeness, recovery, or evidence. This bead owns the exact twenty compositions and their seam contracts after N06.9.2-N06.9.12 make each source transfer self-contained.

## Technical Approach

Register all twenty compounds without collapsing their component axes:

1. **Agent Turn Packet = one-version universe + progressive search + epistemic lattice:** one compact packet summarizes a compatible generation while preserving raw/derived/proposed status, omissions, uncertainty, and stream completeness.
2. **Question graph = scene/provenance graph + coverage + active perception + submodular selection:** questions target evidence that changes a decision, with hard predicates, expected gain, feasibility, cost, and do-nothing.
3. **Spatial MVCC = immutable geometry tiles + read/write/negative witnesses + graph conflict refinement:** concurrent reconstruction names exact spatial/basis reads and writes and refines conflicts without missing phantoms.
4. **Branch per hypothesis = content-addressed history + graph branches + deterministic comparison:** alternate loop closures, scales, semantic identities, agents, and policies remain inspectable and merge only by the semantic ladder.
5. **Incremental retraction = capsule stream + signed deltas + factor dependencies:** calibration/loop/claim corrections propagate retractions and fixed-point updates without hidden stale products.
6. **Proof-carrying context packs = progressive retrieval + graph neighborhoods + Pack DNA + anchor continuity:** every token has source/selection/transform/omission provenance and matches the current basis.
7. **Evidence-gain pilot guidance = graph algorithms + coverage/detectability + obligation verification:** one primary manual instruction and fallback link a question to predicted and later observed gain, cost, safety, refusal, and reconciliation.
8. **Owned model/media workers = Asupersync regions + sealed sidecars + object manifests + reconciliation:** external stacks are useful but untrusted, bounded, cancellable, network-off by default, and incapable of direct authority/publication.
9. **Custody graph = root-last publication + ATP + RaptorQ + provider-neutral object IDs:** large evidence transfers economically with stable roots, explicit durability/custody grades, repair proof, and full restore.
10. **Semantic absence = negative MVCC witness + authorized coverage + detectability + search completeness:** not-found becomes a scoped defensible claim only under compatible observation and recall bounds.
11. **Agent accretion = episode capsules + surprise + Eidetic memory + Doodlestein qualification:** lessons influence future proposals only through evidence, held-out replay, shadow, clamped canary, no-regression, and rollback.
12. **Locally qualified self-description = registries + generated proof documents + exact source closure:** capabilities/help/examples report what this exact machine/profile has proven, including negative and unavailable states.
13. **Multi-agent safe parallelism = region ownership + leases/fences + branch isolation + semantic reservations:** agents expose work and coordinate without filename locks, stale publication, hidden queues, or last-writer authority.
14. **Cost-aware reconstruction = operation witnesses + expected-loss policy + predicted/actual episode ledgers:** compute, storage, tokens, operator/flight time, risk, and evidence gain become jointly measurable; correctness gates remain fixed.
15. **Forensic replay = immutable evidence + deterministic lab + decision/complexity certificates + span-preserving reports:** failures are reproducible from exact roots/schedules/decisions rather than narrated from memory.
16. **Adaptive but non-bypassable operation = policy epochs + hard invariant ceiling + canary rollback:** adaptation chooses effort/order/cache/ranking but cannot weaken privacy, authority, scale, coverage, freshness, custody, recovery, or evidence.
17. **One narrow waist = FastMCP presentation + typed semantic core + context profiles:** broad capability projects through eleven operations; transport/profile changes do not create new semantics or mutations.
18. **Root-last handoff = context pack + active obligations + sealed immutable object:** replacement agents receive exact state, indeterminate work, recovery, ownership, and next steps without transcript dependence.
19. **Topology-aware semantic resolution = geometry + connectivity/cuts + multimodal observations:** room/portal/equipment/access hypotheses use spatial topology and evidence/counterevidence but never let clustering resolve claims alone.
20. **Stopping as certified decision = value of information + coverage + hard predicates + budget ledger:** stable completion or no-useful-action is proven; unresolved debt remains visible when work stops for cost, safety, or missing evidence.

For each compound record canonical ID/name, component versions, owning WP/tasks, prerequisites, input/output schemas, shared anchor, authority/trust/failure boundary, reference implementation, optimized/advisory lane, terminal predicate, recovery, Agent Turn Packet projection, and admission/rollback evidence. Verify the mapping against all 48 WPs, six vertical slices, CD-01..CD-32, and steps 1..21. Reject superficial imports: naming a crate/subsystem after a sibling, source presence, a process exit, a graph-shaped cache, a generic search box, mutable checkpoint, cancellation-by-drop, rendered report, model confidence, receipt-only cloud copy, or hosted workflow cannot satisfy a compound.

## Acceptance Criteria

All twenty compositions have one explicit seam owner and dependency closure with no cycle, missing component, duplicate authority, alternate mutation plane, or semantic collapse. Each has positive and negative end-to-end proof and a cold-agent benefit. Component mechanisms remain independently testable and replaceable.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/check_cross_project_compositions.py` and `scripts/e2e/cross_project_compound_contracts.sh`. Static tests validate exact 20-row inventory, owners, component/version roots, reachability, no forbidden crate paths, unique authority, tests/gates, vertical-slice availability, and rejected-imitation fixture. E2E exercises representative happy/fault paths for every compound, including stale anchor, partial search, retraction, branch conflict, worker crash, corrupt transfer, insufficient absence coverage, memory bypass attempt, stale lease, canary regression, transport replacement, handoff with indeterminate effect, topology counterevidence, and certified stop.

Logs retain compound/component/owner IDs, source/registry/work-graph/crate roots, shared anchors, operations/effects/obligations, capabilities/authority, component receipts, seam transitions, budgets/timings, omissions/counterevidence, output digests, recovery/rollback, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

A compound is justified only when the integration creates a user-facing or proof capability. Do not create ceremony-only bridges. Preserve each component’s authority and failure boundary even when they share storage or scheduling infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: All 20 cross-project compounds have canonical contracts, owning WPs, prerequisites, trust and authority boundaries, reference paths, admission evidence, Agent Turn Packet projections, negative fixtures, and no superficial-import shortcut; their dependency overlay is acyclic and preserves all component distinctions.

title: WP-000/N06.9.14: Prove bidirectional retirement and cold-agent execution without plan Markdown
description:
## Background

This is the terminal proof for document retirement. Counts, filenames, stable-ID occurrence, high lexical similarity, or completion of individual transfer beads cannot show that a future implementation agent has enough context. The proof must test both directions and actual cold-agent behavior while deliberately withholding all plan Markdown.

## Technical Approach

1. Seal the exact 74-document manifest and digests: 63 core/product/policy/architecture/operator/target/provenance sources from N06.9.1 plus eleven deep dives from N06.9.2-N06.9.12.
2. Export the complete Bead graph using `br` and canonical registries/schemas. Normalize each material source requirement and each bead contract into stable fingerprints while retaining source spans solely as provenance.
3. **Forward proof:** every source requirement resolves to self-contained Bead text, canonical ID, unique/integrated owner, dependency closure, public projection, acceptance predicate, unit/property/differential/fault/E2E tests, logging receipt, evidence boundary, migration/recovery, and honest current status.
4. **Reverse proof:** every Bead deliverable, dependency, public claim, gate, test, status, algorithm/mechanism, and emitted vocabulary resolves to originating requirements and machine authority. Detect invented scope, orphan work, circular rationale, and a gate justified only by itself.
5. Compare all registered product and agent IDs, 48 WPs, 240 standard lifecycle children, nine N06 children and fourteen N06.9 grandchildren, six slices, CD-01..CD-32, steps 1..21, 27 acceptance scenarios, research mechanisms/families/compounds, target crates, TEST/SLO/QL/GATE records, and current IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.
6. Run semantic contradiction checks: incompatible state axes/lifecycles, old versus canonical operations/schema names, profile bounds, validate/verify, native oracle maturity, device observation/effect authority, B/BET namespaces, subsystem aliases, crate DAGs, dependency policy, publication/durability/effect ladders, source fact versus target, and unsupported capability claims.
7. Select representative ready/future beads from constitution, evidence, media/time/calibration, geometry/scale, semantics/coverage, custody/search, agent protocol, device research, graph algorithms, fault lab, release, and every research-transfer child. Give a cold scripted agent only `br show`/dependency output and machine registries.
8. Require the agent to state user outcome, rationale, exact inputs/outputs/anchors, prerequisites, prohibited shortcuts, algorithm/state semantics, edge/fault/recovery cases, required code/doc/status surfaces, exact tests, log/receipt fields, terminal predicate, and safe next step. Score omissions by criticality; any missing authority, privacy, scale, coverage, custody, indeterminate-effect, recovery, or evidence boundary is a hard failure.
9. Mutation-test the retirement proof by deleting or weakening one requirement at a time. Diagnostics name source path/heading/fingerprint, expected owner/field, dependency/gate/test, and suggested repair without consulting a transcript.
10. Publish an append-only superseding coverage receipt through `br` comments stating roots, counts, unresolved items, and why original Markdown can be treated as provenance. Do not delete original documents; retirement means implementation independence, not history erasure.

## Acceptance Criteria

Forward and reverse coverage are complete and contradiction-free at the requirement level. No mapping terminates at a filename, broad epic, count, transitive dependency, or source quote. Every representative cold agent chooses the minimum-cost safe action, refuses unsafe shortcuts, identifies proof and recovery, and leaves a sufficient handoff without plan Markdown or transcript. All negative mutations fail with stable actionable diagnostics. Any unresolved item keeps N06.9 and N06 open.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/check_document_requirement_retirement.py` and `scripts/e2e/bead_handoff_without_plan_docs.sh`. Static/property tests cover manifest/digest drift, heading/fingerprint extraction, forward/reverse uniqueness, dependency reachability/cycles, registry/schema/ID parity, fact/design/hypothesis/target classification, status truth, exact research inventories, named tests/logs/recovery, and contradiction rules. Mutations remove an algorithm family, rejected imitation, state transition, privacy rule, negative fixture, authority gate, log field, source closure, owner, dependency, acceptance scenario, or current-evidence limitation.

The E2E uses deterministic case selection plus fixed high-risk cases, with Markdown paths denied. Logs retain corpus/bead/registry/schema/work-graph/source roots, selected bead and dependency closure, question/expected/actual fields, critical omissions, safe-action/refusal/recovery decisions, tests and receipts identified, token/time budgets, output digests, mutation diagnostics, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

This gate is intentionally adversarial. If the agent must infer a protocol fact, reopen the owning bead and add the missing contract. Original documents remain valuable provenance, but they are no longer an execution dependency only after this proof passes.
## Explicit Terminal Dependency and Contradiction Addendum

This proof has direct blocking edges from N06.9.1, all eleven N06.9.1 domain children, all eleven deep-dive imports N06.9.2..N06.9.12, and the compound integration N06.9.13. It cannot run or close on the strength of parent membership alone.

The contradiction suite additionally verifies: exactly 22 graph-algorithm semantic families; geometric/visibility is present; stable GALG-020 temporal and GALG-021 submodular IDs are not renumbered; explicit source ordinals map family 20 geometric/visibility, 21 submodular, and 22 temporal; FrankenGraphDB Strata remains the source mechanism and FDGR Atlas its qualified analogue; and every concrete semantic asset gate, rendition class, pilot-stage boundary, privacy class, restore/delete state, and current maturity named by the eleven core-domain children reaches an owner and executable proof.

The current planning graph has 340 open beads: 1 program, 9 workstreams, 48 WP epics, 240 standard lifecycle tasks, 6 vertical-slice tasks, 9 direct N06 tasks, 14 N06.9 direct children, 11 N06.9.1 domain children, and 2 other program/graph tasks. Counts are diagnostics only; closure still requires requirement-level forward/reverse proof.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic forward/reverse audit and representative cold-agent E2E prove all 74 Markdown documents are requirement-complete in self-contained Beads plus machine registries, with no source-only intent, contradiction, orphan, false status, missing test/log/recovery, or transcript dependency. The terminal node is directly blocked by all 11 core-domain children, all 11 deep-dive imports, and compound integration; graph-family cardinality/stable-ID/source-ordinal and Strata/Atlas contradictions are explicit hard failures. The contradiction suite also requires exactly ten abstraction levels L0..L9 and rejects the legacy nine-level count, missing/merged/renumbered levels, or any cross-level bypass.

title: WP-000/N06.9.2: Import the complete Asupersync correctness model
description:
## Background

Asupersync is part of FDGR correctness because work ownership, cancellation, pressure, time, replay identity, and external effects determine whether an evidence result is trustworthy. Importing only an async executor or adding `&Cx` parameters would miss the semantics. The transfer has nine mechanisms plus a dependency/admission decision.

## Technical Approach

Freeze and assign every mechanism:

1. **Region ownership and quiescence.** Every spawned task/process/stream belongs to an explicit region. Region completion means descendants are drained or accounted for; no detached background work, orphan subprocess, or hidden queue may outlive its authority/budget scope.
2. **`Cx` authority, budget, time, and replay identity.** `&Cx` carries cancellation, deadlines, budgets, pressure/admission, trace/schedule identity, and capability context across orchestration seams. Pure scalar geometry remains runtime-free. Dropping context or fabricating a new root is a typed error.
3. **Cancellation = request -> drain -> reconcile -> finalize.** Cancellation is not an exception or immediate success. Use monotone potential/progress certificates, retain partial artifacts as nonpublished evidence when allowed, reconcile authoritative external state, and emit terminal cancelled/partial/indeterminate truth only after descendants drain.
4. **Two-phase effects.** Prepare a deterministic sealed intent and preconditions before dispatch; persist effect identity and attempt state; dispatch only under current fence/capability; then observe/reconcile before retry or completion. A lost response can be indeterminate and must never be blindly repeated.
5. **Four-valued outcomes and indeterminacy.** Separate success, failure, cancellation, and indeterminate outcome; preserve stage-specific request/process/output/effect/publication states. Process exit or transport acknowledgement never proves semantic completion.
6. **Pressure, admission, and deterministic QoS.** Admit work by declared resource class/budget/priority and deterministic policy. Adapt effort or degrade/refuse explicitly; never weaken correctness, privacy, authority, scale, coverage, freshness, or evidence gates under pressure.
7. **Deterministic laboratory, schedule exploration, and fault injection.** Virtualize time/schedule choices; record seeds and choice traces; explore cancellation and crash at every yield/effect/publication boundary; minimize failures; prove real/lab semantic parity and descendant drain.
8. **ATP immutable object-graph movement plane.** Large artifacts move as sealed content-addressed objects/manifests with backpressure, repair/erasure options, exact roots, and receiver verification. ATP is not mutable shared memory or an authority shortcut.
9. **Anytime-valid monitoring.** Progress/health estimates may update during a run, but optional stopping and partial samples cannot launder correctness. Reports identify sample/epoch, confidence method, threshold, omissions, and whether the terminal predicate has actually been met.

Bind the import to fdgr-runtime/orchestration, obligations, process-region tree, object transfer/custody, lab, and agent ledgers. Asupersync belongs at orchestration/effect seams, not inside every math/codec kernel. Reject Tokio/Rayon adoption, detached tasks, cancellation by dropping a future, “process exited 0” completion, unbounded channels, nondeterministic admission ties, or a lab that tests a different implementation.

The final admission gate requires: region-tree introspection; cancellation matrix at all boundaries; two-phase effect and lost-response reconciliation; pressure/deadline/budget cases; deterministic replay/minimization; ATP integrity/backpressure/repair; anytime-monitor statistics; and public Agent Turn Packet projection of active work, budget, uncertainty, recovery, and terminal state.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every mechanism has a canonical contract, owner WP/crate boundary, typed states/errors, deterministic reference behavior, rejected shortcut, and test evidence. No work can escape a region; no effect can bypass prepare/persist/fence/dispatch/observe/reconcile; cancellation and indeterminacy remain agent-visible; pure kernels remain independent of Asupersync.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_asupersync_transfer_contract.py` and `scripts/e2e/asupersync_region_effect_lifecycle.sh`. Unit/property tests cover region tree invariants, `Cx` propagation, budget monotonicity, deterministic tie breaks, potential functions, four outcomes, effect idempotency, ATP manifest/root integrity, and anytime-valid receipts. Fault E2E injects cancel, deadline, pressure, crash, descendant fork, lost response, duplicate dispatch, corrupt transfer shard, receiver restart, and publication kill points.

Logs retain case/seed/schedule, region/parent/child IDs, `Cx` authority/deadline/budget/pressure fields, intent/effect/attempt IDs, preconditions/fences, process and observation stages, object roots/shards/repairs, drain/reconcile result, timings, digests, omissions, and terminal semantic verdict.

## Considerations

The transfer is semantic, not branding. Use the smallest orchestration seam that needs runtime context. External workers remain untrusted sidecars and recommendations remain authority-free even when their lifecycle is perfectly managed.
acceptance_criteria: All nine Asupersync mechanisms, their rejected superficial imitations, dependency boundary, final admission gate, and agent-loop implications have explicit FDGR owners and deterministic cancellation/effect/pressure/lab evidence without detached work or runtime leakage into pure kernels.

title: WP-000/N06.9.3: Import the complete FrankenSQLite evidence-MVCC model
description:
## Background

The FrankenSQLite transfer is not “use a database.” FDGR needs multi-version evidence and derived state whose readers can name exactly what they saw, whose writers prove what they invalidated, and whose conflicts refine by semantic/spatial scope. The source defines eleven load-bearing mechanisms.

## Technical Approach

1. **Multi-version evidence, not one mutable twin:** immutable generations/capsules and named snapshots preserve originals, observations, refined states, claims, branches, and publication roots; “current” is a small explicit root.
2. **Spatial and evidentiary MVCC:** transactions bind evidence root, geometry/semantic basis, spatial cells/handles, policy/profile, and validity interval. Mixed or stale bases fail closed.
3. **Read, write, and negative witnesses:** positive reads record versions/ranges/objects; negative reads prove an authorized query found no qualifying member under a bounded domain; writes declare affected identities/ranges/cells and expected predecessors. Absence still requires coverage/detectability.
4. **Hierarchical conflict refinement:** begin conservatively at project/generation scope, then refine conflicts through object, spatial tile/cell, graph neighborhood, claim/question, and field/range witnesses. Refinement may increase concurrency but cannot miss a true conflict.
5. **SSI-style dangerous structures for derived claims:** detect cycles of read/write/negative dependencies that could make individually valid derivations jointly impossible; abort/rebase a deterministic victim and retain a certificate.
6. **Deterministic short publication coordinator:** expensive computation happens outside the commit critical section; final validation and root swap are bounded, ordered, fenced, and replayable. No long model/geometry job holds publication authority.
7. **Semantic merge ladder:** exact-equal reuse -> compatible disjoint merge -> monotone evidence union -> deterministic recomputation -> explicit conflict/branch/human adjudication. Last-writer-wins is never the default for evidence or claims.
8. **Branches as reconstruction hypotheses:** loop closures, scale bases, semantic identities, model proposals, agents, and experiments can diverge on immutable common history; comparison and merge retain basis and counterevidence.
9. **Recovery and truth hierarchy:** immutable objects/capsules and sealed roots outrank caches/indexes/derived views; restart reconstructs only from verified roots, quarantines partial state, and records repair/successor epochs.
10. **VFS/storage abstraction without semantic leakage:** storage backends implement bytes/durability/atomicity capabilities behind provider-neutral identities; higher layers never infer semantic completion from an engine acknowledgement.
11. **Conflict/regime telemetry as advisory policy:** measure conflict classes, aborts, refinement effectiveness, hot ranges, and replay cost to tune plans; telemetry cannot relax serializability/evidence gates.

Assign these contracts across evidence ledger, object graph, branch/hypothesis manager, question/plan ledgers, spatial handles, publication coordinator, custody, and deterministic lab. Reject a single mutable scene row, hash-map-order commits, hidden cache truth, SQL/ORM authority leakage, negative queries without witnesses, long write transactions, or semantic last-writer-wins.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every read/result/publication names its snapshot and witness set; every mutation declares a write footprint and predecessor; dangerous structures have deterministic diagnosis/retry; branches and merges retain all evidence; recovery chooses verified roots over convenience state; telemetry remains advisory. All eleven mechanisms have explicit WP owners and Agent Turn Packet projections.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_evidence_mvcc_transfer.py` and `scripts/e2e/evidence_mvcc_branch_recovery.sh`. Deterministic reference tests cover positive/negative/write witnesses, phantoms, spatial refinement, SSI cycles, victim choice, short-root publication, every merge rung, branch compare/rebase, crash recovery, VFS substitution, and advisory telemetry. Faults include stale snapshot, mixed scale/calibration, partial root, cache ahead of root, disk full, concurrent agents, false negative witness, provider acknowledgement without durability, and repair from corrupted replica.

Logs retain transaction/snapshot/root/branch IDs, evidence and basis anchors, read/write/negative witness sets, conflict graph/certificate, deterministic order/victim, merge rung, publication stages, recovery source, storage capability, digests, timings/budgets, omissions, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

An embedded store may implement pieces later, but the semantic contract must be frozen independently first. Database availability, ACID labels, or successful commit calls do not prove FDGR evidence correctness.
acceptance_criteria: All eleven FrankenSQLite mechanisms are mapped to canonical FDGR evidence/branch/ledger contracts with deterministic snapshot, witness, conflict, merge, recovery, and telemetry tests; no mutable-current-twin or storage-engine shortcut can erase provenance or create unsupported authority.

title: WP-000/N06.9.4: Import the complete FrankenFS custody and publication model
description:
## Background

Filesystem and object-store behavior is scientific truth for FDGR: partial visibility, weak durability, path escape, damaged replicas, or deletion of the last original can invalidate every later result. The FrankenFS import contains twelve mechanisms plus a publication kill matrix.

## Technical Approach

1. **Staged, visible, durable are distinct:** a byte/object may be locally staged, namespace-visible, and durably committed at different times; receipts state the strongest proven level and never imply more.
2. **Coherent root-last publication:** materialize and verify all immutable children first, then atomically publish one small root/manifest pointer. Readers ignore unrooted partials; restart adopts or quarantines them by explicit policy.
3. **Content-addressed custody with tiny mutable root:** objects are immutable and digest-addressed; the mutable surface is a fenced project/generation root plus auditable successor history.
4. **Rooted path capabilities:** all local paths resolve beneath an opened root capability; reject absolute paths, `..`, symlink/hardlink/reparse escapes, special devices, TOCTOU swaps, and platform-normalization ambiguity.
5. **Capture spool crash state machine:** Reserved -> Receiving -> SealedPayload -> Indexed -> RootReferenced -> Durable -> Replicated, retaining truncated/partial segments as explicitly classified evidence, never as originals.
6. **Copy-on-write checkpoints and branches:** checkpoints share immutable objects, name exact roots/policy, and support cheap branch/rollback without mutating history.
7. **Repair = plan -> seal -> revalidate -> apply:** build an authority-free repair plan from verified evidence, seal inputs/targets, revalidate preconditions/fences immediately before application, publish a successor, and retain damaged evidence.
8. **RaptorQ repair and adaptive refresh:** erasure parameters are versioned and content-rooted; repair proves reconstructed byte identity; refresh responds to measured loss/temperature but cannot silently rewrite identity or policy.
9. **Scrub, proof of retrievability, custody grades:** distinguish LocalStaged, LocalDurable, ReplicaReceiptOnly, ReplicaReadbackVerified, MultiFailureDomainVerified, RepairQualified, RestoreCampaignQualified; sampling/receipt is not full restore.
10. **Temperature-aware storage/cache policy:** hot/warm/cold placement and cache eviction use measured access/cost while preserving pin/retention/custody requirements and rebuildability.
11. **Virtual twin filesystem as derived view:** human-friendly paths project immutable object-graph state; they are rebuildable views with provenance, not canonical mutable truth.
12. **Same-binary experiments and explicit evidence dimensions:** runtime-selected storage/repair/cache arms use one binary and identical semantic inputs; compare correctness first, then performance with exact source/toolchain/hardware/policy/sample receipts.

The crash matrix injects failure before/after reservation, object creation, write/fsync, rename/manifest seal, child verification, root publication, root durability, replica upload, provider receipt, readback, repair, and cleanup. Each point defines visible state, restart action, retained evidence, and whether publication/durability is proven.

Reject “rename means durable everywhere,” mutable in-place roots, provider-specific IDs in semantic state, path string sanitization without capabilities, repair that overwrites damaged bytes, receipt-only restore claims, cache-as-truth, or deletion while any retention/claim/replica/restore predicate is open.

## Acceptance Criteria

All twelve mechanisms and every crash point have canonical states, capabilities, recovery rules, owners, public receipts, and deterministic tests. Original evidence remains recoverable; no partial root is visible; visible never aliases durable; repair and deletion are fenced and witnessed; provider substitution fails closed.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_custody_publication_transfer.py` and `scripts/e2e/custody_kill_restore_campaign.sh`. Unit/property tests cover path attacks across supported platforms, spool transitions, root reachability, COW branch identity, repair plan sealing, RaptorQ reconstruction, custody-grade monotonicity/demotion, temperature policy clamps, and derived-view rebuild. Run every crash-matrix kill point plus disk-full, lost fsync, corrupt shard, wrong key, stale fence, provider substitution, receipt-without-readback, replica loss, last-original deletion attempt, and full clean-room restore.

Logs retain object/root/project/generation IDs, path-capability root and normalized components, spool state, byte counts/digests, fsync/rename/root stages, custody grade, replica/provider/key IDs, repair parameters and proof, restore roots, fault point, timings/budgets, omissions, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

Storage optimizations may change placement and effort, never evidence identity or required proof. Preserve partial/damaged artifacts as classified evidence when policy permits; never let them silently satisfy a complete-original predicate.
acceptance_criteria: All twelve FrankenFS mechanisms and the publication crash matrix are owned, typed, and tested; staged/visible/durable, root-last publication, custody, repair, restore, path capability, and deletion semantics cannot be collapsed or inferred from provider/process success.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Temperature-tier detail retained from the FrankenFS transfer: T0 volatile compute covers disposable feature/solver scratch; T1 hot durable covers active spool, recent keyframes, and pose deltas; T2 warm derived covers depth/spatial/semantic candidates with cache plus replica; T3 sealed derived covers converged geometry, indexes, and exports; T4 irreplaceable cold covers originals, calibration evidence, and receipts with multiple failure domains plus repair; T5 reproducible cold covers models, benchmark corpora, and generated reports rebuildable by manifest. S3-FIFO, ARC-like, segmented LRU, and learned policies are candidates rather than doctrine. Same-binary trials must compare hit rate, bytes read, tail latency, write amplification, and rebuild cost while preserving semantics, full-basis cache keys, authority/freshness isolation, and deterministic outputs.

title: WP-000/N06.9.5: Import the complete Frankensearch progressive-retrieval model
description:
## Background

Search in FDGR is a decision-support and evidence-navigation system, not a text box. It must retrieve across immutable scene/evidence generations, exact lexical terms, model-produced vectors, graph neighborhoods, space/time, questions, coverage, and authority while explaining partiality and producer identity. The transfer has twelve mechanisms.

## Technical Approach

1. **Staged fast then refined answers:** emit a bounded early result from cheap exact/indexed lanes, then monotone refinements or explicit retractions as slower graph/spatial/semantic verification completes. Every event names completeness and basis; early never masquerades as final.
2. **Immutable search generations:** build segments against one exact evidence/scene/schema/model/policy root, seal counts and producer identities, verify, publish/activate atomically, pin readers, then retire the previous unpinned generation with rollback available.
3. **Hybrid retrieval without score-scale confusion:** lexical, vector, graph, spatial, temporal, authority, coverage, and recency lanes keep raw score/type/calibration; combine only through a registered deterministic policy such as reciprocal-rank or an admitted policy with exact epoch, tie breaks, and explanation, never raw-score addition.
4. **Exact lexical engine as a first-class capability:** identifiers, serials, OCR text, filenames, ontology labels, error IDs, and quoted terms have deterministic tokenization, normalization, phrase behavior, postings, positions, field scope, and exact fallback independent of embeddings.
5. **Vector storage and producer identity:** every embedding binds model artifact, runtime, preprocess, dimension, dtype, normalization, domain, license, source object/span, and basis. Mixed or unknown producers fail closed or search separately; vector similarity is not semantic truth.
6. **Graph, spatial, lexical, and semantic retrieval in one planner:** a typed query plan traverses evidence, scene, question, and provenance graphs; spatial handles; time; lexical indexes; and semantic proposals while enforcing capability, privacy, authority, and cost budgets.
7. **Attention ranking as an operational product:** rank unresolved questions, contradictions, stale or high-risk claims, incomplete obligations, coverage gaps, and high-value evidence by expected decision impact and cost; use hysteresis and preserve suppressed debt. Ranking remains advisory.
8. **Active-perception retrieval:** answer which evidence or view would reduce uncertainty using questions, geometry, visibility, coverage/detectability, costs, safety, and feasible manual actions; return fallback or no-action when value is insufficient.
9. **Absence and recall certificates:** not-found results identify searched generation, fields, space/time, producers, coverage/detectability, filters/budgets, recall limits, and authorization. Only qualified certificates support scoped absence; hidden utilities remain unknown.
10. **Progressive streaming for agents:** versioned events carry query/result/generation IDs, stable items/ranks, additions/retractions/updates, watermarks/completeness, budgets, continuation/recovery, and terminal status. Replay is deterministic and cancellation drains producers.
11. **Rebuildability and activation rollback:** indexes derive from immutable canonical roots, rebuild reproducibly, verify before activation, and can roll back to a prior good generation. Corrupt or stale indexes never become truth.
12. **Performance architecture:** immutable segments, safe memory mapping or zero-copy views, bounded candidate stages, filter pushdown, full-basis caches, runtime-selected one-binary arms, and measured latency/recall/cost only after semantic parity.

Reject one opaque relevance score, mixed vector producers, mutable in-place indexes, embedding-only fallback, unqualified absence, nondeterministic ties, progressive responses without retractions/completeness, or activation based only on process exit.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every result and event is anchored to an immutable generation and producer set; score components and deterministic combination are inspectable; exact lexical fallback works; cross-modal plans enforce authority/privacy; absence is scoped and certified; streams terminate/recover honestly; rebuild and rollback are proven. All twelve mechanisms have owners and Agent Turn Packet/context-pack projections.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_progressive_search_transfer.py` and `scripts/e2e/search_generation_progressive_absence.sh`. Reference tests cover tokenizer/postings/phrases, vector producer partitions, hybrid fusion/ties, graph-spatial filters, attention hysteresis, active-perception/no-action, certificate bounds, event replay/retractions, segment seal/count verification, activation/rollback, cache basis, and one-binary semantic parity. Faults include corrupt segment, stale generation, dimension/model mismatch, omitted lane, authorization change, cancellation, budget exhaustion, activation crash, pinned prior generation, low detectability, and adversarial score scales.

Logs retain query/plan/generation/segment/item/event IDs, canonical roots, lane scores/producers, filters/capabilities, coverage/detectability, rank policy/tie break, completeness/watermark, budget/timing, activation/rollback, omissions, digests, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

Progressive output improves latency only if retractions and incompleteness are explicit. Search proposes context and evidence; it cannot resolve claims or grant authority.
acceptance_criteria: All twelve Frankensearch mechanisms are assigned to FDGR query/context/attention owners with deterministic generation, scoring, completeness, fallback, progressive-stream, rollback, and performance evidence; search results cannot hide basis, producer, omissions, or absence limitations.

title: WP-000/N06.9.6: Import the complete Franken Markdown proof-document model
description:
## Background

FDGR reports, explanations, protocols, robot help, handoffs, and evidence citations are operational interfaces. Losing source spans, accepting unbounded parsing, publishing inconsistent siblings, or rendering model text as authoritative corrupts provenance. The transfer has twelve mechanisms.

## Technical Approach

1. **Exact bytes and source spans:** retain original byte digest, encoding, newline policy, and half-open byte spans through tokens, syntax nodes, diagnostics, rendered anchors, citations, and edits. Normalized text is derived and never replaces source evidence.
2. **Arena-based bounded nonrecursive parsing:** use an iterative parser/state machine with explicit node, depth, token, input, output, and diagnostic budgets; avoid recursion and quadratic adversarial paths; refuse or truncate deterministically with typed offsets.
3. **Clean-room grammar ownership:** register supported grammar/version/extensions and precedence from independent specifications and reference corpora; do not acquire hidden dependency or unapproved copied-code behavior.
4. **Restartable incremental parsing:** checkpoints at safe block boundaries carry grammar state and source digest; edits restart at the earliest affected checkpoint and converge byte-for-byte with a full parse.
5. **Diagnostics as structured evidence:** stable code, severity, span, context, expected, and recovery fields; deterministic ordering/deduplication; versioned machine schema; exact source anchor. Diagnostics never exist only as strings.
6. **One deterministic semantic model, multiple outputs:** HTML, text, terminal, JSON, NDJSON, MCP, robot, and report views derive from one typed model with registered escaping, ordering, IDs, and equivalence rules.
7. **All-or-nothing sibling publication:** render all siblings to staging, verify cross-links, digests, and schemas, then root-last publish one manifest. Readers never see mixed generations.
8. **Taint and authority separation:** user, model, OCR, and imported content remains tainted data; rendering cannot execute active markup or commands, grant capability, resolve claims, or rewrite protocol facts. Escaping and sanitization are target-specific and testable.
9. **Compact auditable render/codec primitives:** small deterministic escaping, entity, URL, span, table, wrapping, and serialization kernels with golden vectors and bounded allocation.
10. **Browser/WASM parity without ambient effects:** the pure renderer works natively and in browser/WASM; filesystem, network, time, and randomness enter only through explicit host adapters; semantic outputs match.
11. **Protocol-documentation co-generation:** schemas and registries generate operation/state/error/profile help and examples; drift fails validation; examples are executable conformance fixtures using lower snake_case and the `fdgr.` plus registered-name plus `/1` schema identity rule.
12. **Quantitative claims linked to checked artifacts:** tables, metrics, and thresholds cite exact machine receipts and query/root; generation rejects stale, missing, or mismatched artifacts and keeps negative results and limitations.

Reject merely selecting a Markdown library, ASTs without byte spans, recursive/unbounded parsing, human-only diagnostics, separately authored robot docs, trusted active markup, partial sibling upload, ambient-time/random output, or performance tables without evidence identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every output is deterministic, bounded, span-preserving, taint-safe, and rooted to one semantic generation; sibling outputs publish atomically; native/WASM parity and generated-protocol drift checks pass; numerical prose resolves to exact evidence. All mechanisms have owners and honest maturity.

## Test Plan

Create `scripts/test_proof_document_transfer.py` and `scripts/e2e/report_protocol_atomic_publication.sh`. Exercise independent conformance and adversarial corpora, incremental/full differential edits, nesting/size/output bombs, malformed encodings, stable diagnostics, cross-render equivalence, native/WASM goldens, tainted active-markup and command strings, sibling kill points, schema/example drift, and stale/missing quantitative receipts.

Logs retain source/document/grammar/generation IDs, byte digests/spans/checkpoints, budgets and peak allocations, diagnostic codes/order, sibling digests/links, taint/escape decisions, artifact/query/root IDs for claims, publication stages, timings, omissions, and terminal verdict.

## Considerations

Readable prose is not authority. Self-description must expose current evidence and unavailable capability, and historical source bytes remain available when a corrected rendering supersedes them.
acceptance_criteria: All twelve Franken Markdown mechanisms are assigned to report/protocol/self-description owners with exact-byte/span, bounded parse, deterministic multi-output, taint/authority, atomic publication, WASM parity, and quantitative-artifact tests; generated prose cannot become an unsupported fact.
